**Issue #1759 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #1759: Patch: the AI keeps its own position switches in the beam, so a losing attacker can stand down
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

In practice the AI almost never moves one of its units to Defense Position on its own turn — even when that unit cannot win its next fight and Defense would keep it alive (Defense grants Taunt and +1 Armor). Its own suggestion machinery tries position switches dead last and usually discards them before simulating a single one, while the opponent it imagines does get to try them. After the change the AI can choose to stand a unit down, the way a real player does.

## Why

`in_move_order` puts every `SwitchPosition` in the last tier — behind hero attacks, trades, plays, powers, activates, answers and other attacks (`crates/ai/src/candidates.rs:592-633`), and `expand` truncates to `branching: 6` below the root (`crates/ai/src/search.rs:104-115`), so a mid-line switch survives only when fewer than six earlier-tier moves exist. The asymmetry is sharp: the imagined opponent gets up to `AI_REPLY.defense_switches: 4` explicit ATK→DEF trials every reply step (`crates/ai/src/reply.rs:362-379`, `config.rs:730`), while the seat's own turn may hold none. `position_grants: 0.0` (`config.rs:407`) compounds it — the static eval reads Defense's Taunt/+1 Armor as roughly nothing (`evaluate.rs:128-148`), so a switch looks like a pure attack loss. `lethal_moves` already recognizes that switches matter for Deft (`lethal.rs:71-80`). Concrete misplay: the AI ends its turn with an unused attacker in Attack facing a bigger enemy unit; a real player parks it in Defense and it survives — the AI's unit dies.

## Proposal

Append up to K `SwitchPosition` actions after `expand`'s truncation, the way `EndTurn` is preserved (`search.rs:111-114`), optionally with a modest nonzero `position_grants` screen so the eval reads Defense's defensive value. A puzzle test asserts the switch is chosen on a losing-Attack board.

## Where it lands

`crates/ai/src/search.rs` (`expand`), `crates/ai/src/candidates.rs` (tier ordering), `crates/ai/src/config.rs` (`AI_SEARCH`, `position_grants`); a puzzle under `crates/ai/tests/ai/`; measured by `cargo jackioh gate`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A named puzzle: an unused attacker facing a bigger enemy ends in Defense Position
- [ ] Switches survive truncation without unbounded branching (K is a named constant)
- [ ] `cargo jackioh gate` stays clean at smoke size
- [ ] No hidden-information read — the switch logic uses only what the seat may see

## Size and risks

Small — roughly 30-60 lines plus a puzzle. The risk is decision time in fat states, bounded by K and measured against the decision budget; a weight change needs gate evidence, not a hunch.

- [ ] [`in_move_order`](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-1759/crates/ai/src/candidates.rs#L592) in [`crates/ai/src/candidates.rs`](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-1759/crates/ai/src/candidates.rs) orders ATK -> DEF switches before DEF -> ATK.
- [ ] `unused_attacker_facing_a_bigger_enemy_ends_in_defense_position` puzzle test passes.
- [ ] `position_switches_survive_truncation_up_to_named_constant` unit test passes.
- [ ] [`crates/ai/tests/ai/policy.rs`](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-1759/crates/ai/tests/ai/policy.rs) expansion tests pass.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` passes cleanly.
- [ ] `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes cleanly.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check` passes cleanly.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh gate` stays clean at smoke size.
- [ ] No hidden information is read by candidate or search logic.

## 6. **Risks.**
- **Branching explosion in wide states:** Adding unbounded switches would multiply beam evaluations exponentially. Mitigated by bounding switches to a small named constant `AI_SEARCH.position_switches` (value 2), keeping total branching per expansion bounded by `width + K + 1`.
- **Hidden information leakage:** AI candidate generation and search must never peek at opponent hidden cards (Rule 7). Mitigated because position switch queries only inspect public `unit_view(state, unit).position` on the active player's own visible field units.
- **Tuning regression from weight changes:** The proposal mentions optionally screening `position_grants`. However, modifying `AI_EVAL.position_grants` affects static evaluations across all AI decisions without sufficient empirical data. Mitigated by keeping `AI_EVAL.position_grants = 0.0`: the opponent's reply simulation (`reply_score`) already correctly recognizes that the unit with +1 Armor survives the trade while the unit in Attack dies, so `SwitchPosition` is selected without perturbing global evaluation weights.

## 7. **Open questions.**
None. All requirements, constant names, bounding rules, and test assertions are fully specified from the engine and AI architecture.
```
